## How to read this report

- **Rate rule** (NFR-QUAL-8): a rate metric passes when its mean across seeds clears the floor by
  more than one sample standard deviation (≥ floors: mean - SD above the floor; ≤ floors: mean +
  SD below it). One seed, or no observations, is *insufficient evidence*.
- **Observed-zero rule** (NFR-QUAL-8): a zero-tolerance metric passes only with no violation on any
  seed, over at least 300 labeled cases. The bound column gives the one-sided 95% upper bound on
  the true rate (≈ 3/n): a clean run is evidence of a low rate, not proof of a zero one.
- **Relative rule** (NFR-QUAL-14): an engine-intervention type passes when its first-draft
  preference rate's mean across seeds plus one SD is at most the floor, judged only on at least
  300 non-tied pairs per seed; fewer is *insufficient evidence*, never a pass. It is an aggregate
  target: individual messages may still read worse than their drafts.
- A judge-based row is only as good as the judge: before such a run the quality judge is
  calibrated against human-labeled pairs, and a judge whose agreement is below 75% makes every
  judge-based row *report only*.
- A model error during a case is a failed case, never silently excluded. In a suite with a
  model-error row (NFR-QUAL-1's zero-leak suites) it is counted and reported on that row, which
  is report-only, and it is not scored as a disclosure: the suite's floors are judged on its
  completed cases, and a zero-tolerance metric with fewer than 300 completed cases on a seed is
  *insufficient evidence*, never a pass. Model-robustness floors belong to M9 (ADR-164). In
  every other suite a model error counts as a bad observation on each of its metrics. Timings
  are informational: the model may share its machine with other work.
- A floor applies to the configuration this fingerprint names (NFR-QUAL-11); any other
  configuration is unmeasured until it has its own report.

- The private-thought metric reads both turns of a case as the player's character: the scripted prelude that plants the thought (its `think` must be filtered out) and the measured turn, rendered by a character who never held it. A clean run is an observed count with its one-sided 95% upper bound, never proof that no thought can leak.
- The oracle sees a disclosure as one of the fact's listed forms (an exact folded phrase), an echo of the thought's words, or a rewording within one sentence by lemma and stem matching (#575): every content word of a multi-word form in any order and inflection, an emotion word of a listed feeling's family with a word of the fact's topic, or most of the thought's content words. The bound covers those phrasings only: a paraphrase that shares no content word with a listed form, feeling or thought, or spreads over several sentences, is not seen.
- Q-01's ranking is what a render's context receives in order: the located occasion's episodes, the assessments, then the ranked memories. Recall@10 is micro-averaged over every query's relevant beats. Without an embedding model (`--embedding-model`) the vector arm does not run and recall rests on the lexical and alias arms.
- Q-02 resolves each query through the retrieval pipeline's resolve stage, with no model; docs/04 sets no floor, so its rows are report-only.
- Q-03 compares recall of an abstract question with and without the reflection tier; no floor applies (docs/04). Without an embedding model retrieval is lexical, so the arm without reflections finds only deeds that share a word with the question.
- Q-04 is a behavioural backstop to PRIV: it measures the final player-facing output of a turn whose correct answer requires not knowing another character's private fact. A clean run is reported as an observed count with its one-sided 95% upper bound, never as proof that no disclosure can happen; a render the pipeline repaired before the output is reported (`q04.render_repaired`), not counted.
- `smoke.instruction_followed` counts an inflected form of the requested word (plural -s/-es/-ies/-ves, -ed/-d/-ing: "candles" for "candle") as following the instruction; a compound ("candlestick"), another word, or no use of the word fails (#437).
